purpose: Original editorial concept illustration for the Jev blog post; not an official logo, benchmark, model architecture, or product screenshot.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: landscape editorial hero image for a Korean technical blog article about Jev, TypeSafe AI's typed decision model. This is an original explanatory illustration, not an official brand asset, model architecture diagram or benchmark.
Primary request: a beautifully composed, restrained 3D software-system illustration expressing one shared text state branching into three parallel typed judgments, with the three judgment outputs converging into a separate code policy. Wide 16:9 landscape composition, suitable as a crisp blog cover. Clear hierarchy and generous whitespace, readable at thumbnail size.
Scene/backdrop: quiet matte off-white background, subtle gray technical grid, refined editorial tech-magazine aesthetic. Soft studio lighting, restrained charcoal typography with muted blue-green accents, no neon.
Subject/composition: one understated floating card marked 'State' containing abstract text rows; three visibly separate floating cards vertically arranged as parallel branches marked 'Choice', 'Score', 'Noul', each with a small non-numeric abstract distribution or decision icon; thin precise paths from State to all three cards, then from each to one separate final card marked 'Code Policy'. No paths connecting the three judgment cards to one another. Cards have shallow depth and light shadows, polished tactile material, not computer chips. A prominent title 'JEV' and a smaller subtitle 'Typed Decisions' occupy clean space above the composition. The flow is a conceptual software interface, not a physical processor or neural-network reconstruction.
Text (verbatim, exact spelling): 'JEV', 'Typed Decisions', 'State', 'Choice', 'Score', 'Noul', 'Code Policy'. Spell Noul exactly N-o-u-l. Only these seven labels, no other text. Typography should be crisp, clean sans-serif, spacious and high contrast.
Constraints: no official TypeSafe logos, no Claude or OpenAI logos, no claims about speed or accuracy, no latency figures or numeric probabilities, no benchmark charts, no token-by-token writing stream, no robot, brain, GPU chip, circuit-board close-up, screenshots, watermark, or decorative pseudo-code. Not an advertisement. Preserve generous margins and make the complete shared-state -> parallel-judgments -> code-policy composition easy to follow.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the referenced Jev blog cover. Change only the small icon inside the Score card and the small icon inside the Noul card; preserve every word, all card positions, labels, title, connections, background, lighting, colors, margins and framing exactly.
Accuracy correction: Score is an ordinal distribution over discrete levels, not a continuous Gaussian. Replace the current overlapping bell curves in the Score card with exactly three tasteful discrete vertical bars of differing heights, in the same muted teal color. No numbers and no axes labels.
Noul is a binary true/false probability, not a three-state Venn diagram. Replace its current three overlapping purple circles with exactly two separate non-overlapping dots, one slightly darker and one lighter, in the existing muted purple tone. No additional text. Keep the label 'Noul' exactly spelled N-o-u-l.
Constraints: change only these two icons as one semantic-accuracy correction. Everything else stays identical, including 'JEV', 'Typed Decisions', 'State', 'Choice', 'Score', 'Noul', 'Code Policy'. No new words, official logos, figures, watermarks, chips or benchmark claims. Preserve the opaque background and original landscape canvas.
